record.original_question: Let Omega be a bounded convex domain in R^2. Solve the Dirichlet problem div(Du/sqrt(1+|Du|^2)) = 2H in Omega with boundary condition u = 0 on partial Omega under each of the hypotheses |Omega| H^2 < pi, L H^2 < 2pi, and diam(Omega) < 2/|H|.

evidence.quote: A method to find H-surfaces spanning a given curve is by solving the Dirichlet problem (4.1).
div Du/sqrt(1 + |Du|^2) = 2H, in Omega; u = phi, in partial Omega.

Problem 4.1 (4*). Let Omega be a bounded convex domain. Solve the Dirichlet problem (4.1) for phi = 0 under each one of the following hypothesis: (1) |Omega| H^2 < pi. (2) L H^2 < 2pi. (3) diam(Omega) < 2/|H|.

artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question concerning sharp geometric solvability criteria for the constant mean curvature Dirichlet equation over bounded convex planar domains. Known results provide existence under stronger conditions (e.g. $|\Omega|H^2 < \pi/2$ via cylinder barriers and Perron methods), and recent works (e.g. on sharp solvability criteria for mean curvature type Dirichlet problems) treat related but not identical thresholds. No source was found establishing existence under the precise hypotheses $|\Omega|H^2<\pi$, $LH^2<2\pi$, or $\operatorname{diam}(\Omega)<2/|H|$, so the problem appears still open.

status_evidence.title: The Dirichlet problem of the constant mean curvature equation in Lorentz-Minkowski and Euclidean space
status_evidence.snippet: For a convex bounded planar domain Ω with a(Ω)H^2 < π/2, there exists a graph on Ω with constant mean curvature H and boundary ∂Ω.
status_evidence.claim: Existence is known under the stronger condition |Ω|H^2 < π/2, not the weaker |Ω|H^2 < π asked here.

status_evidence.title: Sharp solvability criteria for Dirichlet problems of mean curvature type
status_evidence.snippet: Sharp solvability criteria for Dirichlet problems of mean curvature type in Riemannian manifolds: non-existence results.
status_evidence.claim: Sharp criteria for mean curvature type Dirichlet problems are an active research topic, with the planar Euclidean thresholds in question not yet established.
